findings.rationale: CT's uploaded updates turn strongly anti-aligned with the median from about round 5 (cos -0.71 at round 5, -0.80 to -0.89 later) while update norms grow to about 3x the median. Its local model performance is anomalous at round 20: AUC 0.664 (z=-5.8 flagged), CITL -0.057 (observed risk above predicted), and ECE elevated. Lower AUC with observed outcome rate above predicted matches flipped outcome labels, not a pure prevalence shift. Sex subgroup O/E is about 1.65 and 1.31 in both groups, so the excess is across the board, not confined to one subgroup.

IN's updates point against the median from round 4 onward (cos -0.09 at round 4, -0.34 at round 5, -0.79 at round 6, about -0.6 to -1 thereafter), and norms rise to about 3.5x the median. At round 20 its local AUC is 0.679 (z=-5.6) with CITL -0.077 and ECE elevated (z=+4.4). Observed prevalence is 0.228 against a pooled 0.14. Its Sex subgroup O/E ratios are about 1.4 in both groups, so the miscalibration is across the board. This is the pattern expected from flipped labels rather than prevalence shift, since AUC is also depressed.

KS's updates turn anti-aligned with the median from round 4 (cos -0.52), with cos at or near -1 in several later rounds, and norms grow to about 4x the median by round 18. At round 20 its local AUC is 0.694 (z=-4.8), CITL is -0.061 (z=-4.9), and ECE is elevated (z=+3.1). Observed outcomes exceed predictions in both sex groups (O/E about 1.3 to 1.4), which fits flipped labels rather than a subgroup-specific fault.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed the leads with narrower queries. Three clients (CT, IN, KS) stand out consistently across tools. Their updates point against the median and grow in norm from about round 4-5, and their local AUC is depressed (0.66-0.69 against a federation pooled 0.81). Their observed outcome rates exceed predicted risk in every sex subgroup. Together this fits label noise, so I report them as label_noise with onset rounds 4-5. No drift, missing-artefact or explanation-instability signal was confirmed. Other single-statistic leads (AK Sex subgroup, AR Sex FNR, DC and WY feature tails, SD/NH/PR binary-feature spreads) did not replicate on re-query or were within noise, so they are not reported. The full budget of 20 epsilon was spent.
